findings.finding: Company-level seasonality and momentum imply Q3 revenue of roughly $57-59M against a ~$55.0M consensus: Q3 2025 revenue ($44.4M) ran 5.5% above Q2 2025 ($42.1M), Q2 2026 printed $55.9M with written premium +31% and premium in force $419.0M (+31.8%) at 86% policy retention, while the $55.0M consensus implies a 1.6% sequential DECLINE and only +24% y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue $55.9M vs ~$52.2-53.8M consensus (a 4-7% beat) moved the stock +6.26% (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/NEPTUNE+INSURANCE+%28%24NP%29+Releases+Q2+2026+Earnings%2C+Stock+Rises); Q1 2026 ($37.8M, +29%) moved -3.17%; Q4 2025 +12.74%; Q3 2025 -1.15%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $55.0M sits below Q2's actual $55.9M despite a premium-in-force book growing 31.8%; if the street had modelled the 2025 Q2-to-Q3 seasonality, Q3 estimates would sit at $57-59M. Counter: Zacks' own model flags a likely beat, so a small beat is partly expected, and the company noted a slow real-estate market and storm-driven new-business drag.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 comparison from the Q3 2025 release (https://www.reinsurancene.ws/neptunes-revenue-rises-31-2-to-44-4m-in-q325/); Zacks' beat prediction (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/517880-what-you-need-to-know-about-neptune-insurance-holdings-incs-q3-earnings). Shares the Q2 presentation with the guidance finding.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide of $199M (raised at each of the last prints: ~$186-189M, then ~$195M, then $199M) implies H2 revenue growth of only ~19.5% against 31% in H1, and with Q3 consensus at $55.0M it implies Q4 of ~$50.3M (+15% vs Q4 2025's $43.7M); the guide explicitly assumes a benign hurricane season, which Q3 delivered, so a further raise at Q3 is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide raised at Q2 2026 (to $199M) with a revenue beat: +6.26%. Guide raised at Q1 2026 (to ~$195M per stockanalysis): -3.17%. So a raise has been bought once and sold once.
findings.why_not_priced: A ~15% Q4 growth rate is what the guide plus consensus mechanically implies for a book growing 31.8% in premium in force; if the market expected a material raise the stock would not sit 16% below its high after a July-August drift lower and a BMO downgrade. Counter: a raise is the street's script after three raises, so only a raise above ~$203M likely surprises.
findings.independence: Guide history from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/NP and https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15273503076344832; benign-season assumption per call summary https://stocktaper.com/earningsCallSummary/NP/2026/Q2. Shares the Q2 presentation with finding 1.

findings.finding: No NFIP lapse this autumn: the FY2027 continuing resolution signed in early September runs to December 11 and the NFIP's authority now expires December 11, 2026, so Q4 2026 lacks the 43-day NFIP lapse (Oct 1-Nov 12, 2025) that Neptune said drove agent adoption of private flood in Q4 2025, a tougher Q4 comp for the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (the lapse quarter) print moved +12.74% on 2026-02-18, the name's largest reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The CR is public, but the transmission to Neptune's Q4 new business and guide is a proxy the company has not addressed; if priced, Q4 consensus would already embed sub-20% growth, which is roughly what the guide implies, so partly priced.
findings.independence: CR to Dec 11 signed: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-signs-government-funding-bill-avoiding-shutdown-ahead-midterms ; 2025 lapse dates: https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2026-02-06_IN10835_12414f94d3222990be09e00c31ed2293653ce044.html . Proxy, not company-confirmed.

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, FL on 2026-10-09 (the season's first US hurricane after a record-quiet Q3), with modest flood losses (Moody's RMS: storm surge, inland flood and NFIP ~US$250M of a $2.5-4.5B insured loss), a Q4 demand-awareness tailwind in Neptune's core Gulf/Florida market with little loss burden for its capacity providers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print with a fresh landfall in the quarter; company cited below-average 2025 storm activity as a residual drag on new business.
findings.why_not_priced: Weather-to-demand transmission is unconfirmed until management speaks on the call; the stock's +6.7% 20-day run-up may already partly reflect it.
findings.independence: Moody's RMS flood component: https://www.businessinsurance.com/moodys-rms-puts-hurricane-isaias-best-estimate-at-3-5b/ ; Verisk: https://www.verisk.com/company/newsroom/verisk-estimates-insured-losses-for-hurricane-isaias-could-reach-usd-2-billion/ . Weather proxy.

findings.finding: Florida Citizens' flood mandate reaches its final tranche on 2027-01-01 (all remaining personal-lines residential policies, est. ~720,000 more policies), a Q4 2026 / 2027 demand tailwind for the largest private flood MGA that management may quantify on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not a line the company has broken out in prior prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Long public, so mostly priced; only the company's own read of the uptake would be new.
findings.independence: Citizens' own notice: https://www.citizensfla.com/-/new-flood-requirements-begin-january-1 . Proxy, not company-confirmed.

findings.finding: President & Chief Risk Officer Matthew Duffy sold 84,441 shares on 2026-10-08 at ~$27.88-28.47 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-06-12, after filing a Form 144 on 2026-10-02 for 165,570 shares (~$4.5M) received from an RSU vest on 2026-09-30; he still holds 1.88M shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed pattern; selling holders also sold ~11.3M shares in the May 2026 secondary at $27.50.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 4s are public; a pre-scheduled plan carries little information, so this is small overhang rather than a signal.

findings.finding: A $100M buyback was authorised 2026-04-21 and the company borrowed $24M in Q2 to retire 1.22M shares; with the stock sliding to ~$27.4-28.6 in September-October, Q3 repurchases are plausible and would show in the release (net leverage 2.1x, $233M drawn on a $260M revolver).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buyback authorisation came with the Q1 print (-3.17%).
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 buyback volume is not yet disclosed; whether it happened is an inference.
findings.independence: Q2 buyback funding and leverage from the Q2 presentation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002067129/000162828026048999/q22026-earningspresentat.htm).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was historically quiet in the Atlantic (first season since 1914 to reach Sept 21 without a hurricane), and Neptune has said below-average storm activity drags new-business sales; this is a risk to Q3 new business, though the guide assumed a benign season.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 cited residual storm-driven slowdown yet beat and rose +6.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: Weather is public; the guide already assumed it, so it lands inside guidance and mostly priced.

outside_window.finding: NFIP authority and the federal CR expire 2026-12-11; a lapse then would again push agents to private flood, as the 43-day 2025 lapse did.
FEMA Review Council's recommended NFIP-to-private 'take-out' transition requires statutory change; no enactment dated inside the window.
